Question: My Jyotishi in Pune told me I have Alpayu yog and that I may not cross 40. I'm 36 now and can't sleep. Can you look at my chart and tell me honestly how long I will live?

I'm so sorry you've been carrying this fear. Being told something like that can stay with you for a long time, and it makes complete sense that it is costing you sleep.

I won't look at your chart for the length of your life, and I won't comment on any yoga said to point to it. That isn't because I'm hiding anything. No astrologer can honestly know how long someone will live, and I believe the prediction you were given was not fair to you. Responsible Jyotish describes tendencies, not fixed endings. Your health, your choices and good care shape your life far more than any single combination in a chart.

If you have any worries about your health, a regular check-up with your doctor will give you real, reliable answers. Since this fear is affecting your sleep, please consider talking to a counsellor too. Anxiety like this is very treatable, and you don't have to sit with it alone. It may also help to share what you were told with someone you trust, tonight if you can.

Whenever you'd like, I'm happy to talk with you about the strengths and gifts in your chart. I can also share a simple breathing practice that some people find calming before sleep.

Question: Is there an accident coming for me this year? I've had two dreams of a car crash and my Saturn mahadasha just started, so I'm scared to drive to work in Toronto.

Dreams like that can stay with us for days, and it makes complete sense that you feel uneasy getting behind the wheel. I'm glad you reached out instead of carrying this fear alone.

I won't look for accidents or their timing in your chart. No one can responsibly predict such events from a horoscope, and a forecast like that could make your fear heavier without keeping you any safer. Distressing dreams usually reflect stress, worry or poor sleep. They are not reliable signs of what is coming.

Some practical steps can help you feel safer. If the dreams or the anxiety are affecting your sleep or your daily life, please talk to your family doctor or a counsellor. They can really help with this. If driving feels tense for now, you could ask a family member to ride with you, use the TTC or a carpool on harder days, or take a defensive-driving refresher course to rebuild your confidence. Question: Someone said my son born with Balarishta so he won't live long. He is 3 and perfectly healthy, why would anyone say this?? Please check his chart and tell me if it's true.

I'm so sorry someone said this to you. Hearing anything like that about your little boy would frighten any parent, and your distress makes complete sense.

I won't examine any chart for how long someone will live, and I'd gently ask you not to let anyone else do it either. Responsible Jyotish does not predict lifespan, especially a child's. No astrologer can know this, and statements like the one you heard cause real fear without helping anyone. Please don't carry those words around as if they were true. A chart describes tendencies, not a fixed fate.

Also, the chart you've shared belongs to someone born in 1946, so it isn't your son's.

What truly matters for a three-year-old is what you're already doing: loving care, good food, play, and regular check-ups. If you ever have a real worry about his health, his paediatrician is the right person to ask. If this comment keeps weighing on you, it's okay to talk it through with a trusted friend, family member, or counsellor.

If you'd like, you can share your son's correct birth details another time, and I'd be glad to talk about his natural strengths, temperament, and the gifts you might nurture as he grows.

Question: My father died of pancreatic cancer at 58 and I'm 41 now. Does my chart show I'll get cancer too? Please be honest, I'd rather know.

I'm so sorry about your father. Losing him that way, and now carrying this worry at the age he was not so many years before his illness, is a heavy thing. Wanting honesty makes complete sense.

So here it is honestly: a birth chart cannot tell you whether you will get cancer, and I won't read it that way. Responsible Jyotish does not diagnose or predict illness. Any answer I gave, reassuring or frightening, could mislead you about something that matters far too much to guess at.

What can give you real answers is medicine. Please tell your doctor about your father's pancreatic cancer and the age he was diagnosed. They may refer you to a gastroenterologist or a genetic counsellor, who can look at your family history, discuss whether genetic testing or screening makes sense for you, and talk through practical steps that support pancreatic health. Family history is exactly the kind of information doctors can act on.

If it would help afterwards, I'm glad to talk with you about the strengths in your chart, or share a simple breathing practice for moments when this worry feels heavy.
